newsitem.title: USA: Mich. Gov. announces new renaissance zone options.
newsitem.headline: Mich. Gov. announces new renaissance zone options.

text.p: Michigan will provide loans of up to $5 million and $50,000 technical assistance grants to communities participating in the state's tax-free renaissance zone program, Gov. John Engler has announced.

Michigan will pay interest and principal on the loans for up to five years to spark the creation of business parks and other developments before specific tenants are lined up, Engler announced Thursday.

The loans can be repaid through credits based on the number of new jobs created, but communities will be required to assume the remaining balance if enough jobs are not created at the end of five years.
Communities can use the technical assistance grants to study infrastructure needs in the areas such as extensions of water, sewer and electric lines.

Michigan established the renaissance zone program earlier this year at 11 sites. Properties and economic activity within the districts are exempt from state income, single business and property taxes, as well as local property, income and utility use taxes.
Engler said investors have put $128 million into 28 projects in the zones to date, creating 1,417 to 1,628 jobs.
